clue.text: Greek poetess with an aversion to fools erasing name on biro?

indicators.note: erasing tells us to rub out the pen's brand from the longer coinage

parts.note: saps are fools, so a coinage for fearing or hating them is sap-phobic
Bic is a brand name printed on many ballpoint pens

explanation.surface: A poet who can't stand idiots wipes a name off a ballpoint pen.
explanation.walkthrough: SAPPHOBIC is a made-up word for 'hating saps'; 'erasing' removes BIC, the pen brand (Biro is a British word for a ballpoint), leaving the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the celebrated lyric poet of ancient Lesbos, a woman writing in Greek.

clue.text: Movement as follows lion stopped by head of zookeepers

parts.note: sc., short for scilicet, means namely or as follows

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged in the middle by the following letter

parts.note: a lion is a brave person, a hero

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A lion at the zoo is held back by the senior keeper, with the movement described as follows.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet, 'namely') then HERO 'stopped by' Z, the 'head of zookeepers'. 'Lion' looks zoological; it means a brave person.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively section of a symphony or sonata, one of its movements.

clue.text: Musical flower

definitions.meaning: ... describes catchy music in a pop style

explanation.definitionFit: Poppy is both a bright field bloom and an adjective for tuneful pop-style music.

clue.text: See 25
Dissertation not say in essay, described with what we have here

indicators.note: described in its old sense of drawn round, so the remnant is enclosed by the outer word

parts.note: this is the word for the thing we have here

indicators.note: not says the word say is to be dropped from the word essay

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction for writing a dissertation: leave something unsaid in the essay and describe what is in front of you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' leaves ES; 'described with' uses describe's old geometric sense of drawing round, so the leftover is enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is the long piece of research writing submitted for a higher degree.

clue.text: River hot, shade burnt?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
burnt umber is a brown paint shade, so umber is the shade that can be burnt

explanation.surface: A river so hot that it scorches the colour of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burnt' is no anagram signal: burnt umber is a paint colour, so UMBER is 'shade burnt?'. The Humber is an English estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Humber is the large estuary in northern England formed by the Trent and Ouse.

clue.text: Sound of setter filling puzzle up for speaker

indicators.note: filling means going inside the other letters
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle
a setter is a gun dog, and its bark is a woof

explanation.surface: The crossword setter fills the puzzle with his own voice for a talking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives SUBER, and 'filling' puts the bark inside. 'Setter' looks like the puzzle compiler but is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A subwoofer is a loudspeaker designed to reproduce the lowest bass frequencies.

clue.text: Fine material cut, so lustrous

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: silk is a fine fabric
very and so are both intensifiers

explanation.surface: A fine fabric being trimmed, so shiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' leaves SIL; 'Fine' poses as an adjective but belongs to the fabric phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Silvery describes a shining, bright sheen like polished silver, a lustrous quality.

clue.text: Surrealist dunking fish factory in gin, as weird

indicators.note: dunking means plunging in, so these pieces go inside the jumbled letters
weird signals that these letters come out in a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
the pike is a freshwater fish
a mill is a factory

explanation.surface: An odd picture of a fish factory being plunged into gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' scrambles the fodder so it splits S/IGAN, and 'dunking' sinks the fish and factory between. Milligan was a British comic famed for The Goon Show.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike Milligan, a Goon Show creator, was famed for absurdist, surreal comedy.

clue.text: Approach food items fresh from the frier?

parts.note: chips are fried potato pieces, a food item
food just out of the fryer is hot

explanation.surface: A question about what to call food items just out of the deep fat fryer.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay splits after the S, against the answer's own word break. In golf an approach is a stroke played onto the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip shot is a short lofted golf stroke, the typical approach played onto the green.

clue.text: Vehicle where one after mass transported by people in a ferment

indicators.note: what is transported is carried inside the other letters
something in a ferment is churned up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a mob is a mass of people
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Picture a vehicle carrying someone after Mass through an excited crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a ferment' makes POPEILE, and 'transported by' carries the crowd inside it. 'Mass' looks like church; it is the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The popemobile is the special glass-sided car in which the Pope rides among crowds.

clue.text: See elderly woman briefly reversing pattern in socks

indicators.note: reversing tells us the whole combination is read from the end back

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: gran is short for grandmother, an elderly woman

explanation.surface: Watch Granny going backwards in her patterned socks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims GRAN to GRA; ELY + GRA read back by 'reversing' gives the answer. A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is the stock example.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyle is the diamond-check design traditional on Scottish knitted socks and sweaters.

clue.text: Darling behind my back, swoon

indicators.note: behind places the sweetheart after the other piece
back tells us to read that exclamation from the end

parts.note: eek is an exclamation of alarm, like my!
a lover is a darling, someone loved

explanation.surface: Someone discovers their darling has been going behind their back and swoons with shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is read as an exclamation of surprise; 'back' makes KEE, and 'behind' puts the sweetheart after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to collapse or faint, as a ship capsizes onto its keel.

clue.text: Head bagging new job, I haven't been informed

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: a dome is slang for the head
a task is a job

explanation.surface: A departmental head grabs the new job, and an employee shrugs that nobody told them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a boss but is slang for the skull; 'bagging' holds the new job inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'don't ask me' is the idiomatic shrug of someone who has no knowledge of a matter.

clue.text: A raft travelling south carrying pieces from shore?

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other piece inside
travelling signals that the letters move into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
sand is the granular stuff of the shore

explanation.surface: A raft drifting south laden with flotsam from the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' makes THOUS, which 'carrying' wraps round the beach material. 'Raft' is a boat in the surface but a large number here.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft of things is a great number of them, and thousands means very many.

clue.text: Dubious humming, intro forgotten

indicators.note: intro forgotten tells us the word's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: humming is British slang for smelling bad, as is niffy

explanation.surface: A tune hummed with its introduction forgotten sounds doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' looks musical but is British slang for smelly, as is NIFFY (a niff is a bad smell); 'intro forgotten' drops the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is an informal word for doubtful or of questionable quality.

clue.text: See 9
Bone crusher ultimately in ferment

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the phrase

parts.note: to stir up trouble is to ferment it

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A bone crusher churning things up, like a grinder in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: R, 'ultimately' crusher, goes 'in' STIR UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The stirrup, or stapes, is the tiny stirrup-shaped bone of the middle ear.

clue.text: In need of repair, some girl pinning a dress up

indicators.note: pinning means holding the single letter in place within the others
something in need of repair is broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl's dress needs mending, so she pins it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In need of repair' rearranges SOME GIRL into GLMORISE; 'pinning' holds A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To glamorise is to make something more attractive, embellishing it as one does when prettifying.

clue.text: Tough seafood, starter changed

indicators.note: starter changed tells us the opening letter is swapped for another

parts.note: lobster is a shellfish eaten as seafood

explanation.surface: A restaurant complaint: the seafood was tough, so the starter was changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter changed' swaps the L of LOBSTER for M. 'Tough' looks like an adjective about chewy food; it is a noun, a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a violent hoodlum, and a mobster is a gang member of that kind.

clue.text: Belt out to bind organ, very painful

indicators.note: to bind means wrapping round, so the second piece is enclosed

parts.note: to belt out a song is to sing it loudly
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A belt pulled tight around an internal organ would hurt intensely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bind' wraps the singing round the organ. 'Belt' looks like a strap; it is to sing loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Searing pain is acute and burning, the sharpest kind of hurt.

clue.text: As well for French and English as English rival?

parts.note: aussi is the French word for also, as well

explanation.surface: A linguistic query about phrasing in French and English for a sporting rival.
explanation.walkthrough: England and Australia are sporting rivals, most famously at cricket in the Ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian, the old foe in cricket and rugby, is a stock rival of the English.

clue.text: What we do carelessly in writing about an Amercan state?

definitions.text: What we do carelessly in writing about an Amercan state?

parts.words: What we do carelessly in writing about an Amercan state
parts.note: careless writers drop a letter: the clue itself misspells American, leaving out one of its letters, so we lose our letter from it

explanation.surface: A wry admission that spelling slips creep in when writing about the US.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint is deliberate: in 'Amercan' we MISS OUR I, and those words run together into a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest along the river of that name.

clue.text: Country cabin in block

indicators.note: in places the shelter inside the prohibition

parts.note: to ban something is to block it
a hut is a small cabin

explanation.surface: A cabin in a block, as if describing a mountain retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: HUT goes 'in' BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhutan is a small Himalayan kingdom lying between India and China.

clue.text: On reflection, somewhat grim, a musty taste sensation

indicators.note: On reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, something grim and musty is a taste experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes IMAMU from inside grim, a musty; 'On reflection' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic taste, alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

clue.text: Engine part with nut on screw

parts.note: a nut or crank is an eccentric person
to shaft someone, like to screw them, is to cheat them

explanation.surface: A mechanic's note that an engine part comes fixed with a nut on a screw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' and 'screw' pose as hardware but are a crank (an oddball) and to shaft (to swindle).
explanation.definitionFit: A crankshaft converts the up-and-down motion of the pistons into rotation in an engine.

clue.text: Actually live

definitions.meaning: a broadcast shown ... is live, in real time

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a sentence adverb meaning in fact and a description of real-time coverage.

clue.text: Bill when Charles will reign?

definitions.meaning: a bill is a printed notice stuck up in public
Charles would reign after Elizabeth Regina, known as ER

explanation.walkthrough: Set before Elizabeth II died: ER is her royal cipher, so the time after her is POST-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a public placard or advertisement, and so is a poster.

clue.text: Name dividing Washington and Berlin?

parts.note: two famous Americans share a name, one as surname and one as forename, so it sits between them

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals are a feint: Washington Irving the author and Irving Berlin the songwriter join through the shared name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a forename and surname, linking writer Washington Irving and composer Irving Berlin.
